findings.title: The advertised uniform regret orders discard uncontrolled stability factors
locations: Lemma A.1 p.12; Appendix A.2-A.4 pp.12-17; Appendix A.6 p.22
affected_claims: Matrix regret order under stated convexity/rank/comparator assumptions
findings.actual_problem: The proofs absorb lagged/current preconditioner factors into a constant although the stated assumptions do not control them. The vector algorithm additionally applies a lagged-regret lemma incompatible with its zero initialization. Complete loss sequences make actual regret divided by the advertised factor unbounded.

vector_counterexample.parameters: Fixed d>=2, tau=1, D=1, eta=1/sqrt(2); also exact-sketch tau>=2 variants
vector_counterexample.assumptions: Convex differentiable losses, global gradient cap 1, attained comparator x*=0
vector_counterexample.strengthening: Final loss x_1+sqrt(1+||x+e1||^2)-1 gives a unique optimum x*=-e1 with ||x*||=D and a global gradient cap 2, retaining bounded terminal covariance and divergent regret.

matrix_counterexample.losses: First N losses -X_11; final loss N*X_11+||X||_F^2/2
matrix_counterexample.assumptions: Convex, queried gradients rank one, unique optimum 0, fixed positive epsilon
matrix_counterexample.claimed_factor: At most 25N; ratio at least sqrt(N)/100

findings.strongest_alternative: Read max as min, use intended symmetric fast reconstruction and explicit pseudoinverse; all are accommodated. A uniform gradient cap can restrict the matrix theorem, but the vector counterexample already has one.
findings.why_alternative_does_not_save_original: The vector corrected coefficient at the last step is 1/(N+1), and the exact-sketch case has zero escaped mass. The matrix theorem states no fixed gradient cap. Fixed original parameters cannot absorb unbounded sequence/horizon dependence.

repair.status: Restricted vector repair proved and independently checked
repair.change: Use A_t=delta I+B_tB_t^T+rho I, delta>0 fixed, and ||g_t||<=G fixed
repair.limits: Changes original algorithm and retains explicit ridge/gradient dependence; no matrix repair or empirical invariance established

findings.impact: Damages central mathematical guarantees and any transfer relying on them. Does not refute FD approximation, the separately assumed mirror-descent theorem, all empirical outcomes, or all regularized variants.
findings.later_version: arXiv:2610.16792v1 changes max to min and restores a transpose, but retains relevant updates/conditions and unbounded factors in targeted inspected statements.
